commitResults.messageBody: Move scanner ownership and all user-facing console messages out of Moon so the application entry point delegates UI responsibilities to a focused class. Preserve the existing command behavior and output while establishing the first step toward a more object-oriented design.

commitResults.messageTitle: Set executable JAR name to moon.jar

commitResults.messageBody:
Moon contains a command error line longer than the 120-character limit, and Storage imports do not follow a consistent order.

These violations make the source harder to scan and prevent the project from following the required SE-EDU Java conventions.

Keep the source within the line-length limit and use a consistent import order.

The project needs reusable instructions for Java style and Git messages so future changes follow the same SE-EDU conventions.

Add focused skills for Java code and Git branches and commits, with links to the authoritative standards.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mandate project coding and Git standards
commitResults.messageBody:
Project guidance does not identify the coding and Git standards that future changes must follow.

Require the project-specific Java and Git skills for all code changes, branch names, and commit messages.

Moon cannot search task descriptions by keyword, and the UI test runner does not compile or launch the package correctly.

Users need a direct way to locate tasks, and the planned UI sessions must run independently.

Add case-insensitive find support, test the matching output, and make each UI case use an isolated working directory.

The project lacks automated checks for the SE-EDU Java coding standard.

Style guidance alone does not report violations during normal builds.

Add Checkstyle 14.1.0 with project configuration and suppressions so checkstyleMain, checkstyleTest, and check enforce repeatable checks.

Provide a fit-for-purpose graphical interface for managing tasks.

Reuse the command engine for both the console and GUI so task behavior
remains consistent across interfaces. Configure JavaFX and FXML support,
and add regression tests for the reusable engine.

The JavaFX application now needs a distributable artifact that includes
its third-party runtime libraries.

Document the Java 25 Gradle command, generated file location, bundled
JavaFX dependency requirement, and recommended command for running the
fat JAR. This gives users a repeatable workflow without committing the
generated binary.

The application has several assumptions about task indexes, parsed task
objects, and JavaFX view initialization that should remain true during
normal execution.

Document these invariants with Java assertions and enable assertions for
Gradle run and test tasks so programming errors are detected during
development without treating user input as an assertion failure.

The command processor mixed command recognition, parsing, task mutation,
and response formatting in one long method, making changes harder to
review safely.

Name command syntax constants and move each command operation into a
focused helper so the dispatch method reads as a clear list of supported
commands while preserving the existing behavior.

The persistence format used raw task-type, status, and separator literals,
so the meaning of each value had to be inferred from the surrounding code.

Give each protocol value a descriptive constant name while preserving the
existing file format. This makes the storage contract easier to review and
reduces the risk of changing one occurrence but missing another.

Task serialization and keyword matching are collection transformations, but
were implemented with manual loops that mixed selection with presentation.

Use streams for mapping tasks to their saved representation and filtering
matching tasks. Keep the final numbering loop because it directly expresses
the response format without introducing state into the stream pipeline.

Users need a way to recover from the most recent task-changing command.

Keep one serialized snapshot of the task list before each mutation and
restore it through the existing storage format when the undo command is
requested. This supports additions, deletions, and status changes without
exposing mutable task internals.

Refresh the Moon interface with a responsive night-themed layout, distinct user and assistant message bubbles, and highlighted error responses. Add generated wolf-and-moon artwork and a compact avatar so the visual design remains cohesive across the chat window.

commitResults.messageTitle: Give Moonie a Gen Z personality
commitResults.messageBody: Refresh Moon's CLI and GUI wording with a relaxed task-bestie persona while keeping command guidance clear. Update the farewell test to match the new user-facing response.

commitResults.messageTitle: Harden command and data error handling
commitResults.messageBody: Normalize user input and report missing, malformed, duplicate, and invalid date parameters clearly. Validate persisted task data, reject duplicate entries, and convert file-access failures into recoverable Moon errors. Add regression tests for the new validation paths.

Cover task and event formatting, state-changing commands, search and duplicate handling, storage round-trips, malformed persisted data, and console UI behavior. Keep JavaFX-only classes outside automated coverage because they require a live UI toolkit.
Remove the stale Duke template reference, document Moonie's current setup, and acknowledge the starter template, third-party libraries, generated artwork, and AI-assisted development.
Remove the GUI subtitle and simplify Moonie's welcome and error messages by dropping the requested slang phrases. Update the console UI test to match the refined wording.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename app to Moon and label send control
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the remaining Moonie branding with Moon across the console, GUI, and documentation so the product name is consistent everywhere.

Rename the GUI action button to Send and update the welcome-message test so the visible interface and its verification stay aligned.
